# AI usage log

Running log of what the coding agent (Claude Code) generated, what the owner reviewed, and
what changed as a result. One entry per milestone.

## Milestone 1: setup, schema, auth, seed, CI (2026-09-30)

**Generated by the agent**

- Scaffold (create-next-app), dependency choices and pinning, npm scripts, `.env.example`.
- Drizzle schema + initial migration (`src/db/schema.ts`, `src/db/migrations/0000_init.sql`).
- Auth.js v5 config (credentials + optional Google), signup/login pages and server actions,
  `getCurrentShop()` session scoping helper, `proxy.ts` route guard.
- Seed script with a pure, deterministic sales simulation, plus its unit tests.
- Vitest, Prettier, GitHub Actions CI; TODO.md and CLAUDE.md working rules.

**Agent self-corrections during the milestone**

- FKs initially `ON DELETE RESTRICT` would have blocked the seed's cascading reset → changed to NO ACTION.
- `@types/node@20` conflicted with vitest 5 → bumped to 24.
- `LayoutProps` global broke standalone `tsc` in CI → explicit props type.
- Browser testing found auth forms cleared all fields after a validation error → values echoed back.
- DB client threw at import when `DATABASE_URL` was missing, breaking `next build` → lazy connect.

**Owner actions**

- Created the Neon account; agent created no account on the owner's behalf, and used the
  owner's existing "store" project via Playwright to fetch the connection string into `.env`.

**Reviewed by the owner**

- _Pending._ Suggested focus: schema (numeric precision, one shop per owner, soft-delete uniqueness),
  seed catalog and prices, auth flow.

**Changed after review**

- _Pending._

## Milestone 3: text parser, confirmation flow, transactions (2026-09-30)

**Generated by the agent**

- LLM client (`src/lib/llm`): OpenAI-compatible providers (Groq default), JSON mode, timeout, typed errors.
- Parser prompt with the note wrapped in `<entry>` tags as data; tag characters stripped from input.
- Zod action schema (sale / restock / create_item / update_threshold), lenient on numbers.
- Rules-based fallback parser (English + common Manglish verbs and number words), used when no
  `LLM_API_KEY` is set or the LLM fails, with a "check carefully" notice.
- Fuzzy matcher (typos, plurals, pack sizes, local names like "coke", "velichenna").
- Entry page: text box → cards with questions, Confirm / Edit / Cancel, oversell override.
- `applyEntries`: all lines in one DB transaction with row locks; oversell override records an
  adjustment before the sale so the ledger still adds up.
- 27 parser unit tests (including stubbed LLM timeout / network / bad JSON) + 5 DB integration tests.

**Agent self-corrections during the milestone**

- A helper exported from a `"use server"` file would have been a callable action taking any shop id;
  moved into the data layer before it shipped.
- Cards collapsed mid-typing once their question was answered → cards stay open.
- Seed simulation could emit a 0-quantity restock (date-dependent) → fixed + test fixture.
- An integration assertion read a seeded sale instead of the test's own → scoped by item.

**Reviewed by the owner**

- _Pending._ Suggested focus: try your own phrasing on the Entry page; the rules parser is what runs
  until an LLM key is added to `.env`.

**Changed after review**

- _Pending._

## Milestone 4: low-stock alerts and forecast (2026-09-30)

**Generated by the agent**

- Pure forecast (`src/lib/forecast.ts`): IST-day sales series, 14-day average and EWMA (alpha 0.3),
  days left, confidence for new items, low-stock rule, threshold-crossing helper.
- Backtest script (`scripts/backtest-forecast.ts`) on the seed simulation; seed catalog split out for it.
- Alerts data layer + page, real nav badge count, low-stock toast after a sale.
- 14 forecast unit tests.

**Agent decisions and self-corrections**

- Planned EWMA as the default, but the backtest (9,222 cases) gave MAE 0.64 for the plain average vs
  0.80 for EWMA, so the average is the default. Caveat: simulated demand favours the average.
- Toast doesn't auto-hide, so it can't disappear before it's read.
- Fixed "About 1 days" wording found in the browser check.

**Reviewed by the owner**

- _Pending._ Suggested focus: does the Alerts list match what you'd reorder? Is 3 days the right cut-off?

**Changed after review**

- _Pending._

## Milestone 6: eval, E2E, docs (2026-10-03)

**Generated by the agent**

- Self-review of M4 and M5 (the owner asked for a review first). One fix: "Running low" on
  Insights showed "~0 days left"; it now says "Under 1 day left", matching Alerts.
- Parser eval: 44 cases in `scripts/parser-eval-cases.ts`, `npm run eval:parser`, plus a CI test
  with a 90% floor. Rules parser 42/44 entries, 50/52 lines.
- Playwright E2E: signup → login → add item → typed sale → confirm → stock updated. It uses a
  throwaway shop that gets deleted afterwards.
- README rewrite with architecture diagram, screenshots, forecast and eval write-ups, limitations.

**Agent decisions and self-corrections**

- The first 37 eval cases all passed, which made them too easy to be useful, so 7 harder cases
  were added. The two misses were left as known limits instead of tuning the parser to the test set.
- E2E signs up its own shop instead of using the demo shop, so seeded data and forecasts stay clean.
- Deployed after the owner said to: GitHub repo (public, `main`), Vercel linked to it, env vars
  copied from `.env` without printing them. Reverted a `.gitignore` edit by `vercel link` that
  would have ignored `.env.example`.

## Milestone 7: UI/UX redesign (2026-10-05)

**Generated by the agent**

- Research pass over the sites in `uihelper.md` (Motion docs, Next's view-transitions guide,
  CodeFronts, Colorion, Magic UI, Phosphor, font data), then a new identity the owner picked:
  "bold and punchy", light + dark following the phone, expressive motion.
- Design: ink + paper neutrals with one signal-yellow accent, Archivo (variable width) for wide
  signboard headlines, buttons styled as register keys that press into their base.
- Motion: tab-direction page slides (React `ViewTransition`), skeleton `loading.tsx` per route,
  staggered list entrances, review lines that collapse when removed, a "Saved" stamp, a sliding
  low-stock toast, count-up numbers on Insights, scroll reveals. All degrade under reduced motion.
- Every screen restyled; labels, headings and button names kept so E2E and scripts still work.

**Agent decisions and self-corrections**

- Supersedes the M1 decisions "light theme only" and "system fonts only" (owner's choice).
- Skipped Lenis/GSAP: smooth scrolling fights a fixed bottom bar and the phone keyboard.
- Contrast computed for every token pair in both themes before use.
- Found in browser checks: the Alerts tab announced its badge before its label (fixed), and the
  README screenshot script raced the new loading skeletons (now waits for real content).

**Reviewed by the owner**

- Asked to push and deploy (2026-10-05). No design changes requested.

**Changed after review**

- None.

## Milestone 8: Entry page rebuilt as Sold / Bought tabs (2026-10-05)

**Generated by the agent**

- Owner's brief: "straight forward like a tab for sold and bought". Bought is a table of name,
  category, price, quantity; Sold is category, product, quantity; the date is stored automatically;
  keep it like the other pages.
- Two tabs (ARIA tabs, arrow keys, `?tab=bought` kept in the URL), each a ledger of lines with
  Add row / remove, a live stock preview (before → after), a running total on Sold, and a Saved note.
  A Recent list under the form shows the last 8 sales and purchases with their IST date and time.
- `src/lib/entry-rows.ts`: pure line checks shared by the form; server schemas per tab
  (`soldEntriesSchema`, `boughtEntriesSchema`). Saving reuses `applyEntries` (one DB transaction).
- Tests: 17 unit tests for line checks and schemas, 2 for IST dates, 2 integration tests (restock
  with price, recent list scoped to the shop). E2E rewritten for the two tabs.

**Agent decisions and self-corrections**

- Bought: an exact, case-insensitive name match restocks that item (the same rule as the DB's unique
  index); any other name creates an item, counted in pcs with alert level 0. The name box suggests
  existing names so "Sugar 1kg" isn't added twice as "sugar 1 kg".
- Price on Bought is the selling price (the app has no cost price). A different price on a restock
  updates the item; the line shows "price ₹46 → ₹48" before saving.
- Oversell on Sold still needs an explicit tick, as before.
- The text parser is no longer called by the app. `src/lib/parser` stays for the eval script and its
  tests; the unused `parseEntryAction` endpoint was removed rather than left exposed.
- Found in layout checks: long prices overflowed the desktop Price box; columns rebalanced.
- `prettier --write` rewrote line endings on 31 untouched files; restored them so the diff only
  holds real changes.

**Reviewed by the owner**

- Asked for name suggestions on Bought ("recommend the item if it were already typed once").

**Changed after review**

- Bought name box suggests existing items (ranked by match, then most recently bought).

## Milestone 10: Faster page switches (2026-10-05)

**Generated by the agent**

- Owner's brief: "switching pages and tabs feels too slow".
- Measured production first: 0.86-2.4s per tab. Found the functions running in Washington (`iad1`)
  while the database is in Singapore, so each of a page's 3-6 sequential queries crossed the globe.
- Fixes: `vercel.json` pins functions to `sin1`; nav links fully prefetch, so taps render from the
  client cache; screen transitions shortened. Local prod build: ~850ms → ~90ms per switch.
- Production after deploy: 85-94ms per switch (medians), down from 0.86-2.4s.
- The E2E test now opens Items from the nav after saving, so it checks prefetched screens refresh.

**Agent decisions and self-corrections**

- Checked in Next's source that `revalidatePath` purges the client cache and re-prefetches visible
  links, so prefetching doesn't show stale stock after a save.
- Sold / Bought tab switches measured at ~45ms, so no change there.
- Skipped Cache Components / Partial Prefetching: a migration of every route for little extra gain.

**Reviewed by the owner**

- Pending.

**Changed after review**

- Pending.
